title: Beyond a Recognition of Results
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece argues that leaders who recognize only results, rather than the underlying effort, courage, and creativity that produce them, are missing a major driver of team commitment and engagement. It suggests deliberately broadening recognition to include qualities like persistence, resilience, and innovation, especially after a disappointing outcome, since performers want to know their invisible work is noticed regardless of whether it paid off. The article notes that while praising effort works well with children, adults respond more to recognition of specific qualities like adaptability or vision.
points: Recognizing only results, not the underlying effort and qualities, undermines team commitment.
Performers want their invisible investments noticed and valued, especially after disappointing outcomes.
Recognition should target specific qualities (creativity, resilience, vision) rather than generic effort with adults.
The article frames broad recognition as a free but high-value leadership lever.
quotes: Leaders who only recognize and reward outcomes and results miss a critical link affecting so many of the qualities they want from their team members.
Performers at all skill levels want to know that their under-the-radar investments to achieve success are prized as highly as the success itself.

They go out of their way to recognize and acknowledge, both publicly and privately, the underlying sacrifices, qualities, and energies that help to produce results, even when the outcomes are disappointing.
Recognizing or praising effort, especially with children, is known as a key motivator for future undertakings, but it is less impactful with adults.
Best of all, such recognition is absolutely free, yet worth a fortune to team success.
